title: should canvas `.toBlob()`/`.convertToBlob()` work without a rendering context?

labels.name: needs tests
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires someone to write tests

body:
Calling `offscreenCanvas.convertToBlob()` (and I assume `canvas.toBlob()`) on a canvas without a rendering context works on Firefox, but fails with an exception on Chrome.

I wanted to create a blank/transparent blob URL as a placeholder on a script for one of my personal websites, and I usually test it mainly on Firefox, but I got a report from a Chrome user that it was broken.

Plainly calling `canvas.getContext("2d")` solved the issue for me, but I was wondering whether Chrome’s behavior is against the spec before filing a bug for Chromium.

(As a related note, I think MDN should include a note about this in case Chrome’s behavior is allowed per spec.)

The error Chrome gives is the following:

~~~
InvalidStateError: Failed to execute 'convertToBlob' on 'OffscreenCanvas': "OffscreenCanvas" has no rendering context.
~~~

Related Chromium issues:

- [40756385](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40756385) (`.convertToBlob()` with WebGPU)
- [41361579](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/41361579) (`.toBlob()`/`.convertToBlob()` error handling mismatch)
